newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Ramos confident over Philippine workers in HK.
newsitem.headline: Ramos confident over Philippine workers in HK.

text.p: Philippine President Fidel Ramos said on Sunday he was confident the welfare of the estimated 150,000 Philippine workers in Hong Kong, most of them maids, "will remain protected" after the territory reverts to Chinese rule on Monday.
Chinese officials have sought to reassure Manila the status of the Filipino workers would not be affected by the handover.
But the Philippine Daily Inquirer newspaper said attempts by Manila officials to reassure the Filipino workers that they had nothing to fear about Chinese rule in Hong Kong were pathetic.
It was bad enough that Filipinos, with official encouragement, left the country to look for jobs overseas, it said.
"That Philippine leaders have to plead for their continued employment overseas is a humiliating spectacle unbecoming of a sovereign nation," it said.
Ramos added in a statement that Asia needed a politically stable Hong Kong after the handover to maintain the region's economic growth.
"The economic vitality and political stability of Hong Kong is of critical importance to the continued prosperity of the Asia-Pacific region... and to a vibrant global trade in general," Ramos said.
